title: throughput-regression-continuous-batching-misconfig-scratchpad
body:
Context:
- Users started seeing a ~25-40% drop in tokens/sec for hosted API traffic (baseline toy workload) after runtime change in deploy v2025.01.11 (kernel picker + batching tweaks).
- Affects long-running chat endpoints with average seq_len=512; shorter requests (seq_len<128) largely unaffected.
- Suspected continuous batching config or KV cache behavior change.

Repro notes (local perf harness):
- Harness: tools/perf/harness.py --model redwood-7b --mode streaming --requests 10000 --concurrency 64 --seq 512
- Before change (v2025.01.08): 380k tok/s per GPU, p95 lat 110ms
- After change (v2025.01.12): 245k tok/s per GPU, p95 lat 220ms

Commands tried so far:
- Check current continuous-batching config on node:
  kubectl -n inference get configmap runtime-config -o yaml | yq '.continuous_batching'
- Dump runtime debug logs:
  kubectl -n inference logs runtime-xyz -c runtime --since=2h | rg "batch|kv_cache|kernel" -n
- Run microbench on single model variant with different batching window:
  python tools/bench/run_batching_sweep.py --model redwood-7b --gpu 0 --batch_windows 5,10,20,50 --seq 512

Observed log snippets (raw):
- "[INFO] batching: window_ms=20 max_batch=64 avg_batch=12 flush_count=3120"
- "[WARN] kv_cache: eviction triggered early, entries=12000 threshold=10000"
- "[ERROR] kernel-selection: fallback to generic-kernel for attention, reason=unsupported-seqlen-pattern"
- "[DEBUG] actual_batch_size=1 latency_ms=180 token_service="streaming""

Quick hypotheses:
1) batching.window_ms increase or mis-applied config caused smaller effective batches for long seqs (more time per batch) -> throughput drop.
2) KV cache eviction happening more frequently (eviction_threshold mis-set) causing re-compute of prefixes and extra kernel overhead.
3) Kernel picker fallback: new heuristics mis-detect patterns for seq_len ~512 and picks slower generic kernel.
4) Quantization kernel changes interacting with batch shapes causing lower GPU occupancy.

Small experiments & results:
- Sweep batch window: 5ms -> 20ms -> 50ms
  * 5ms: 320k tok/s, p95=130ms (better than post-change, worse than pre-change)
  * 20ms: 240k tok/s, p95=210ms (matches regression)
  * 50ms: 190k tok/s, p95=300ms (worse)
  => conclusion: window_ms 20 appears to be the regression point compared to previous 8-10ms default.

- Disable KV cache eviction (set eviction_threshold very high) on a single node:
  * throughput improved ~15% vs window_ms=20 baseline
  => kv_cache churn is contributing but not sole cause.

- Force kernel-picker to prefer legacy attention kernel via env: RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=legacy_attention ->
  * throughput returned to ~360k tok/s, p95 ~115ms
  => indicates kernel selection change is a major contributor.

Error snippets to track down (copied):
- "fallback to generic-kernel for attention, reason=unsupported-seqlen-pattern; pattern=16x32x?: detected_stride_mismatch"
- "kv_cache: eviction triggered early, entries=12000 threshold=10000; sample_keys=..."

What changed in the release (investigation notes):
- PR #678 modified kernel selection heuristics to prefer fused_attention when batch shapes are stable and memory footprint low; also bumped default batching.window_ms from 8 -> 20 to reduce syscall overhead.
- Default kv_cache eviction threshold changed by config schema migration in PR #670 (intended to free memory faster).

Working theory (combined):
- Increasing window_ms to 20 caused batches to be more varied in shape for long sequences (mix of short + long within same window). Kernel picker now sees more shape variability -> heuristics decide fused_kernel not beneficial -> falls back to generic slower kernel. Combined with more frequent KV cache evictions this amplifies latency and kills throughput.

Immediate mitigations tried (and status):
- Revert batching.window_ms to previous 8ms on canary pool: throughput back to ~360k tok/s. (TEMP FIX, rolled back to canary only)
- Set RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=legacy_attention for affected fleet (hotfix on 2 nodes) -> good perf, but not safe long-term.
- Increase kv_cache evaporation threshold to previous value -> partial recovery.

Next steps / action items:
- Rollback window_ms change for all hot-path nodes (owner: Liam) - blocked by deploy freeze? check infra schedule. (ETA: asap)
- Add telemetry to kernel-picker decisions (log which heuristic branch picked, batch_shape histogram) (owner: me/Ava)
- Add an integration test for mixing seq lengths in the batching window to detect kernel fallback regressions in CI (owner: Sofia)
- Revisit PR #678 heuristics: prefer stable kernel if seq_len distribution within window has >80% same stride; fall back thresholds too aggressive. (owner: kernel team)
- Evaluate dynamic window_ms that adapts to seq length distribution instead of global config. (product/prod-ops discussion)

Notes to self / debugging breadcrumbs:
- Relevant binary flags: --batching-window-ms, --max-batch-size, --kv-eviction-threshold, RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL
- Useful log queries: rg "kernel-selection|batching: window_ms|kv_cache" -n /var/log/runtime/*.log
- Benchmark script: tools/bench/run_batching_sweep.py (add arg --seed to make runs reproducible)

Open questions:
- Why did kernel picker heuristics regress only for seq_len ~512 and not shorter sequences? Need to capture actual batch_shape hist for failing runs.
- Are there memory fragmentation effects causing the picker to consider fused kernels too risky?

Short-term checklist before wider rollout:
- [ ] Add kernel-picker telemetry (histograms saved to /metrics/kernel_picker/)
- [ ] Rollback batching.window_ms to 8ms for all inference regions
- [ ] Re-run full perf harness across seq 32/128/256/512 to confirm no regression elsewhere
- [ ] Create targeted unit/integration tests to capture fallback-to-generic-kernel cases

Random notes/ideas:
- Maybe try hybrid strategy: small window for long-seq endpoints, larger window for short interactive endpoints. Use routing to separate.
- Consider adding 'shape-stability' probe inside batcher that delays including a request if shape mismatch > threshold (fast path for streaming low-latency).

Appendix (raw commands run):
- kubectl -n inference patch configmap runtime-config --patch '{"data":{"continuous_batching.window_ms":"8"}}' && kubectl rollout restart deploy/runtime
- python tools/bench/run_batching_sweep.py --model redwood-7b --gpu 0 --batch_windows 5,8,20,50 --seq 512 --concurrency 64
- env RUNTIME_FORCE_KERNEL=legacy_attention ./bin/runtime --config /etc/runtime/conf.yaml

Last updated: 2025-02-20 by Ava
